title: Shift compatibility of normalized inverse-image coefficient comparisons
statement: For the normalized independent-universe geometric and coefficient data of def-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-data, let e be already constructed Comparisons(g,nY,nX). Fix coherent scalar shifts whose universal counits commute with shifts. Then each specified derived inverse-image/scalar comparison e.derived(a) commutes with these shifts. No finite-limit assumption on uInv is needed beyond the supplied comparison and exact module inverse-image data; no coefficient map is required to be flat.

proof.text: For a scalar presentation p, transport its homotopy counit along quotientCompQhIso and mapHomotopyCategoryFactors to the natural transformation on complexes whose component is computation(p,P). Every factor, including the functor associators, commutes with shifts when the counit does. The termwise ordinary comparison also commutes with shifts degree by degree.

Form the source computation beta by the scalar counit on Y followed by exact inverse-image factors and the termwise ordinary comparison. Form the target computation alpha by the exact inverse-image factors followed by the scalar counit on X. Their shift equations are compositions of the preceding shift equations.

The equation whiskerLeft(Q,e.hom) followed by alpha equals beta holds on flat-term K-flat complexes by Comparisons.representative. Both sides are natural transformations with source Q followed by a derived functor. Resolve any complex by a flat-term K-flat complex, invert the image of its augmentation under this source, and use naturality to extend the equation to all complexes.

Every derived object is isomorphic to Q(P) for a flat-term K-flat resolution P. At P, beta is invertible because the given scalar computation is invertible. The comparison e is invertible, so its equation makes alpha invertible too. Compose the two sides of the comparison shift equation with shift(alpha(P)) and precompose with the invertible image of Q shift. The source and target computation shift equations identify the words; cancel both isomorphisms. Naturality transports equality from Q(P) to the arbitrary object. This proves compatibility with every integer shift without assuming that an evaluation detects derived equality.
